chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The meal is complete when it gathers four characteristics: when it is from permissible [food], when there are many hands [partakers], when it is named [Bismillah] at its beginning, and when Allah is praised (Alhamdulillah) at its end.'

key_terms.الْأَيْدِي: Hands (referring to the number of people eating)

ai.seo_question: What are the four conditions that make a meal complete according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi highlights that a meal is spiritually complete only when it combines legal purity (halal), communal sharing (katharat al-aydi), and ritual remembrance (dhikr). The invocation of God's name at the beginning sanctifies the act, while praising Him at the end acknowledges the blessing, transforming a physical necessity into an act of worship. This framework underscores the integration of fiqh (jurisprudence) and adab (etiquette) in daily life.
